equity_bridge.note: FY25 balance sheet, US$36m (2024: US$35m); flows are consolidated so the NCI stock is deducted once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 organic guidance midpoint (6-8%), consistent with the medium-term framework (high-single-digit organic) and the 5-year revenue CAGR of 9.4% which includes c.2-3%/yr of acquired revenue
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (17.4%, FY2020 US$2,281m -> FY2025 US$5,090m) diverges >30% from revenue (9.4%) and EPS (11.8%): book value is inflated by acquisition goodwill (illion, ClearSale, Audigent/NeuroID; US$1.2bn of acquisitions in FY25 alone) and the FY2020 base was depressed by buybacks. It is not a growth signal and was not used; the 3-year equity CAGR (8.3%) sits with revenue.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue: FY2021 US$5,372m -> FY2023 US$6,619m -> FY2026 US$8,425m. EPS is Benchmark EPS (USc 103.1 FY21, 135.1 FY23, 179.8 FY26) because statutory EPS carries acquisition-intangible amortisation and non-cash FX remeasurements. Owner FCF = reported FCF (OCF - capex; Benchmark FCF for FY26) - SBC: FY2021 1,066-106 = 960; FY2023 1,090-129 = 961; FY2026 1,600-147 = 1,453. Owner-FCF CAGRs track reported FCF CAGRs within 1pp: SBC is c.1.7% of revenue and growing in line with it, so stock is not funding the growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Experian delivers FY27 guidance (6-8% organic, +50bps margin) and the medium-term framework thereafter: Ascend cross-sell and Consumer Services monetisation of 215m+ free members keep organic growth high-single-digit into FY29 before fading as US credit penetration matures, Benchmark EBIT margin climbs from 28.6% to c.31% as cloud dual-running ends and AI productivity gains land, capex normalises from 8% to 7% of revenue, working capital stays a c.12% drag on incremental revenue (93% OCF conversion), and the US$1bn buyback keeps the count flat. The AI-disruption fear that de-rated the shares in 2026 proves overdone: >90% of revenue stays tied to proprietary bureau data that LLMs consume rather than replace. The CFPB case settles for practice changes and a fine absorbed within the margin path.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI opportunity management sized at >US$15bn (agentic-commerce identity with Visa/Cloudflare, Ascend governance and fraud automation, LLM-embedded marketplaces live with ChatGPT) converts into a re-acceleration: organic growth runs 8-9% through FY29 with the US mortgage and card cycle recovering as rates fall, Brazil B2B returns to growth, and Consumer Services wins share from Credit Karma on the marketplace. Operating leverage plus the completed cloud migration lift the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 41.5% (Benchmark EBIT c.32.5%), capex falls to 6.8% of revenue, and terminal growth is 3.5% reflecting structural credit-penetration growth in LatAm and Asia-Pacific.
scenario_narratives.bear: Agentic AI and open-banking data networks erode the bureau's pricing power: Decisioning and Marketing Services get commoditised by LLM-native tools, Consumer Services loses marketplace economics to Intuit/Credit Karma, and a US/Brazil credit downturn (the Board's 'increasing' macro risk) cuts B2B Financial Services volumes. Organic growth drops to 3% from FY29, the pre-SBC EBITDA margin compresses from 37.5% to 35% as Experian keeps investing (capex held at 8%) to defend data and platform relevance while losing price, the CFPB suit ends in a costly consent order and mandated dispute-handling changes, and the exit multiple is capped at 15x FCF (a structurally slower, higher-leverage business at 2.3x net debt/EBITDA pro forma). No scenario hits the terminal-value zero floor.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Experian is valued as an unlevered owner-FCF stream in USD, converted to pence at the spot rate. The value rests on three things the components make auditable: organic growth fading from guided 7-8% to 3% over ten years, a pre-SBC EBITDA margin that expands only at the guided +30-50bps/yr pace and then plateaus, and a capex/D&A pair that normalises to 7.0%/6.5% as the cloud migration completes. SBC (c.1.7% of revenue) is expensed and the share count held flat, so the two concurrent US$1bn buybacks add nothing to value here -- they are the mechanism for the flat count. Leases are charged once as operating cost and excluded from net debt. Risk is charged once, in the flows and the 25/50/25 weights, not in a scenario-specific WACC. Terminal value is Gordon at 8.5%/3.0% (18.7x, below the 20x cap) in base and bull and capped at 15x in bear.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI/agentic disintermediation of bureau data and decisioning -- the bear axis; if proprietary data loses pricing power the margin path reverses rather than plateaus
US, Brazil and UK credit-cycle sensitivity -- Financial Services is c.53% of revenue and the Board flags macro risk as increasing
CFPB FCRA lawsuit (filed January 2025, in discovery) -- fines, redress and mandated dispute-handling changes in the largest market
Rising net interest (FY27 US$250-260m) and leverage to 2.3x pro forma for buybacks and M&A -- less balance-sheet room if a downturn arrives
FX: USD flows against a GBp quote; a 5% GBP move shifts every pence value c.5% with no change in the business; BRL/GBP translation moves Benchmark EPS c.2c/1c per 10%

Anchor vintage: net debt and diluted shares at 31 March 2026 are derived from the FY26 prelim deck, not a filed balance sheet; SBC for FY26 is an H1-scaled estimate -- replace with the FY26 annual report when extracted
Discount-rate sensitivity: with Gordon binding at 18.7x in base, a 1pp move in WACC moves the base value by roughly a fifth

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (EXPN.L, GBp) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2203-3707p. FX from Yahoo GBPUSD=X at the date in inputs.fx_note; parity check against the EXPGY ADR.
data_sources.financials: EXPN.L_Metrics.csv (FY2016-FY2026, US$m) from the annual reports FY2016-FY2025 (EXPN.L_Annual_FY2025.txt: cash flow statement, note 13 D&A split, note 27/29 borrowings and lease obligations, note 18 diluted shares), the H1 FY26 interim (cash flow and net debt summary, note 19 net debt) and the FY26 preliminary results deck (EXPN.L_Annual_FY2026.txt: revenue, Benchmark EBIT, OCF, FCF, net debt/EBITDA, WANOS, FY27 guidance).
data_sources.qualitative: EXPN.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): business model, moat, AI-disruption and CFPB risks, FY27 guidance, bull/bear cases.

inputs.sbc_source: FY26 estimate: H1 FY26 share-incentive charge US$73m (H1 FY26 cash-flow summary) scaled by the FY25 full-year/H1 ratio (127/65); FY25 cash-flow add-back US$127m (EXPN.L_Annual_FY2025.txt cash flow statement); plus c.US$5m 'Other payments on vesting of share awards' (financing, FY25 US$5m) = sbc_incl_equity_taxes. FY26 annual report not yet extracted -- replace with the actual when it is.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate is PENCE PER USD = 100 / GBPUSD 1.3233 (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-09 21:29 UTC) = 75.569. The engine multiplies every USD per-share figure by it, so the canonical intrinsic_value, weighted_iv and entry_price are in GBp and comparable to current_price; the *_usd siblings hold the model-currency figures. Parity check: OTC ADR EXPGY (1 ADR = 1 ordinary share) closed US$35.57 on 2026-10-09 vs LSE close x 1.3233 / 100 = US$35.49, 0.2% apart -- rate, direction and quote basis confirmed.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T15:49:18Z (LSE regular close; Yahoo chart meta). 52-week range 2203-3707p.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-03-31 (derived from the FY26 preliminary results deck: net debt / Benchmark EBITDA 1.7x on Benchmark EBITDA c.US$3,015m and a c.US$0.5bn increase in net debt from the filed US$4,684m at 2025-03-31, giving company-defined net debt c.US$5,150m incl. c.US$140m lease obligations; last FILED balance sheet is H1 FY26 at 2025-09-30: net debt US$5,180m, lease obligations US$140m, cash US$288m). Replace with the FY26 annual report figures when extracted.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-03-31 (derived: FY26 WANOS 913m per prelim deck; H1 FY26 WANOS 915m with c.17m shares bought back in FY26 -- US$725m at c.US$42 -- weighted to H2, gives c.899m in issue net of own shares at year end, plus c.7m dilutive awards per the FY25/H1 FY26 EPS notes = 906m diluted. Cross-check: FY27 WANOS guidance 880-885m is consistent with 899m less a further US$1bn programme executed through FY27.)
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted (basic in issue net of own shares + dilutive share-incentive awards, c.5-8m per the EPS notes), held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count. The US$1bn FY27 buyback programme is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat (and in practice shrinks it); it is value-neutral here and is NOT credited, so the valuation does not depend on buyback execution.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Risk-free 5.24% (US 10-year Treasury, ^TNX 2026-10-09), ERP 4.5%, beta 0.9 (quality data compounder, moderate credit-cycle exposure) -> cost of equity c.9.3%. Marginal pre-tax cost of debt c.5.5% (BBB+/Baa1; FY27 net interest guided US$250-260m on c.US$5.2bn, average rate 3.6% on legacy fixed coupons, marginal higher), after 26% tax c.4.1%. Market weights c.86% equity / 14% debt (market cap c.US$32bn vs net debt c.US$5.2bn) -> WACC c.8.6%, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is priced in the flows and the weights, not stacked in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal US$41m + interest US$7m in FY25, c.US$55m in FY26 = 0.6% of revenue) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease obligations (c.US$140m) are EXCLUDED from net_debt (company-defined net debt c.US$5,150m less c.US$140m leases = US$5,010m). D&A for the tax shield is Benchmark D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (FY25: 547 - 43 = 504 = 6.7% of revenue) so the lease is charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (US$36m book, c.US$4-5m of profit). Flows are consolidated; the NCI book value is deducted once in equity_bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company, non-US filer -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations (a) currency and (b) leases). Experian is a global credit bureau / data and decisioning business with 19+ years of organic growth, 28.6% Benchmark EBIT margin and >90% cash conversion -- a cash-flow stream, not a book-value or AFFO business. FY0 is FY2026 (year to 31 March 2026) on the preliminary results deck: revenue US$8,425m, Benchmark EBIT US$2,407m (28.6%), Benchmark EBITDA c.US$3,015m (EBIT + c.US$608m D&A, H1 FY26 D&A US$300m scaled by the FY25 H2/H1 ratio), Benchmark OCF US$2,221m (93% conversion), Benchmark FCF US$1,600m. reported_fcf is Benchmark FCF, which is LEVERED (after net interest c.US$185m and tax paid); the component build is unlevered and discounts at WACC, so last_fcf is an anchor and audit trail, not the projection base. The pre-SBC EBITDA margin that the ebitda_margin_path starts from is (3,015 + 142) / 8,425 = 37.5%: Benchmark EBIT already expenses SBC, so the path adds it back and sbc_pct_path charges it explicitly. Working capital is a persistent cash drag at Experian (FY24 -32, FY25 -54, FY26 c.-150 implied by 93% conversion; H1 seasonally -275) so wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE (-12% base) -- the 93% OCF conversion guidance is reproduced by the base components (Y1 Benchmark OCF / EBIT c.93%). Cash tax is modelled at the guided c.26% Benchmark rate on unlevered EBIT (cash taxes paid ran 23% of Benchmark PBT in FY25, 31% in FY24 on a one-off). Interest income (US$14-19m) is not stripped: the company is a net borrower, so there is no cash pile to double-count. Buyback_cash is the US$725m actually executed in FY26 (US$529m of it under the January 2026 US$1bn programme); the new US$1bn programme to June 2027 is an authorisation, not spend. Anchors: price is the 2026-10-09 LSE regular close (not after-hours); net debt and share count are both at 31 March 2026, derived from the FY26 prelim deck as described in balance_sheet_date / share_count_date -- the FY26 annual report (statutory cash flow, balance sheet, EPS note) has not been extracted and should replace both when it is.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 = guidance: 6-8% organic (7% mid) + c.1% completed-acquisition contribution, FX taken as neutral (guided 1-2% either way). Then a 0.5pp/yr fade from high-single-digit organic toward 3% terminal as US credit-penetration and Consumer Services audience growth mature; no further M&A assumed.
base.margin_rationale: FY26 pre-SBC EBITDA margin 37.5% (Benchmark EBIT 28.6% + D&A 7.2% + SBC 1.7%). +50bps in FY27 per guidance, +50bps FY28-29 (medium-term framework +30-50bps/yr as cloud dual-running ends and AI productivity gains land), fading to +20bps and flat at 40.0% from FY33, i.e. Benchmark EBIT margin plateaus c.31%.
base.capex_rationale: c.8% of revenue in FY27 per guidance, trending to the c.7% medium-term framework level as cloud migration completes; D&A (software amortisation dominated) lags capex and settles at 6.5%, below capex because the business is still growing.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default and bull cut to 25% from 35%. Bear: the AI-disintermediation axis is a genuine structural tail that the market is actively pricing (shares -19% YTD at one point on record results), the CFPB FCRA suit is unresolved in Experian's largest market, and the Board itself flags credit-cycle risk as increasing while net debt/EBITDA heads to 2.3x pro forma. Bull: requires several independent things to go right at once -- AI-enabled products scaling to material revenue, a US lending-cycle recovery, Brazil B2B re-accelerating, and continued share gains in Consumer Services -- immediately after management stepped FY27 organic guidance down from 8% to 6-8%. Base at 50%: guidance delivery is the best-evidenced path given 19+ consecutive years of organic growth and two years of margin targets exceeded.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
